correctness.rationale: For all q,t, all words of length t+1 embed into t increasing copies and the final permutation, and one-symbol repetition gives a missing length t+2. An embedded prefix of length t+1 needs t+1 increasing copies exactly when all its t comparisons are weak descents. The remaining last two symbols occur in final permutation iff increasing there. Weak-prefix multiset enumeration yields the binomial weighted formula. verify.py exhaustively checks all permutations q<=7 using integer arithmetic and direct scattered-subsequence checks for 99 small cases; no finite test substitutes for the universal proof.

value.rationale: Exact SAS cardinalities in a structured family with arbitrary number of universal arches are compactly encoded as weighted permutation dot products. The first genuinely nonlinear case has a natural, nontrivial spectral realizability boundary: at q=6 and 7 only immediate-extremum gaps survive, whereas q=3,4,5 have many internal holes. This supplies a complete finite calibration for the unresolved general nonlinear support question, rather than an arbitrary digit sample; t=1 classical support is explicitly separated from novelty.
